When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks. Our findings demonstrate that multiple, co-existing transcriptional programs shape the phenotypic diversity of EwS and suggest that the balance between these networks may have important implications for clinical outcomes and targeted therapy development.
nfb3c4e069e67: Local adaptation has been demonstrated in many organisms, but the traits involved and the temporal and spatial scales at which selection acts are generally unknown. We carried out a multi-year study of 200 accessions (natural inbred lines) of Swedish Arabidopsis thaliana using local field sites and a combination of common-garden experiments that measured adult survival and fecundity, and selection experiments that measured fitness over the full life cycle. We found evidence of strong and variable selection, with particular genotypes favored more than fivefold in certain years and locations. Fecundity showed evidence of classical local adaptation, with accessions generally performing better closer to their home. However, relative to other accessions, southern ones usually had the highest fecundity—but were far more sensitive to harsh winters and slug herbivory, which strongly decreased both survival and fecundity. Furthermore, accessions originally sampled on beaches had low fecundity in all common-garden experiments, but massively outperformed all other accessions in the selection experiments, presumably due to an advantage during seedling establishment associated with their very large seeds. We conclude that local adaptation in A. thaliana reflects strong temporally and spatially varying selection on multiple traits, generally involving trade-offs and different life-history strategies, making fitness difficult to predict and measure.
n961fa323122b: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST+ vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST+ vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.
ne0ca8f373016: Mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene are a defining feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) and impose metabolic and stress adaptation requirements that may create exploitable vulnerabilities. Prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) inhibitors have been explored as therapeutic agents in CRC; however, their mechanisms of action and off-target effects remain elusive. Serendipitously, we found that Molidustat, a PHD2 inhibitor, induced cell death in human APC-mutant CRC cells. Ablation of PHD2 alone did not affect cell viability, suggesting an off-target mechanism. Using thermal proteome profiling and chemical proteomics, we identify glutathione S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) as a previously unrecognised off-target of Molidustat and demonstrate direct inhibition of its enzymatic activity. Genetic ablation of PHD2 alone did not phenocopy the cytotoxic effects of Molidustat, whereas combined loss of PHD2 and GSTP1 induced synergistic proteomic changes associated with cell-cycle suppression and apoptotic signalling. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses further revealed energetic and metabolic perturbations specific to simultaneous GSTP1 and PHD2 loss. Consistent with these findings, APC-mutant mouse organoids displayed selective sensitivity to Molidustat that was not reproduced by hydroxylase inhibition alone, supporting a synthetic lethal interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in APC-mutant contexts. Together, these results identify a functional interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in a subset of CRC and suggest that off-target engagement of GSTP1 contributes to the anti-tumour activity of Molidustat.
nb794c330c37a: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features—one that enhances and one that suppresses activity—around an elevated baseline firing rate. By combining neuronal recordings with functional digital twin models—deep learning-based predictive models of biological neurons—we were able to systematically identify each neuron’s preferred and non-preferred features. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. We show that this encoding strategy is conserved across species, present in both primary and lateral visual areas of mouse cortex. Dual-feature selectivity is consistent with recent anatomical evidence for feature-specific inhibitory connectivity, complementing the feature-detector principle through circuit mechanisms in which selective excitation and inhibition may together enhance the representational capacity of the neuronal population.
neada78d98c9d: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the ‘fight-or-flight’ response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) – an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. Transcriptome analyses indicated that SBV infections, and DWV infection with OA treatment, activated honey bee metabolic pathways, and that SBV-infected bees had greater expression of genes involved in OA synthesis, unless treated with OA. These results provide mechanistic insight for virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight, which may have consequences for foraging efficiency, colony health, and virus transmission.
n125b24145100: Biologics and immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment of autoimmune conditions and cancers. However, safety data regarding use during pregnancy are limited. Clinicians are left to weigh the potential benefits of treatment with frequently unknown risks to the pregnant patient and developing fetus. These therapies do not cross the placenta during the first trimester; thus, they are unlikely to cause teratogenicity. Use later in pregnancy has the potential to immunosuppress the neonate, which could lead to infection and inadequate vaccine response. These large molecules are minimally transferred into breastmilk and are mostly compatible with nursing.
n0468515ca3f7: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na + transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. This primary effect is thought to drive both K + secretion and Cl − reabsorption; however, the underlying mechanism has remained obscure and the dual regulation has generated an enigma often referred to as the aldosterone paradox. Here we propose a model for regulated K + secretion centered on local regulation of ENaC in the late distal convoluted tubule and early connecting tubule. In this segment, the MR is constitutively activated by glucocorticoids rather than by aldosterone, and yet ENaC activity and K + secretion through the renal outer medullary K + channel (ROMK) are not constitutive but, rather, are highly regulated. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K + secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K + ] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na + -Cl − reabsorption is favored. This revised paradigm resolves the aldosterone paradox and has important implications for hypertension, potassium disorders, and potentially medical therapies.
n02ffad94b8a7: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Peptide and nonpeptide GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), as well as a combined GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), agonist are approved for type 2 diabetes, weight reduction, and other indications. GLP-1RA therapy can be complicated by upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea and vomiting. Delayed gastric emptying secondary to GLP-1RAs may be influenced by drug pharmacokinetics, associated neuropathy, and development of tachyphylaxis with repeated dosing. A theoretical risk of pulmonary aspiration from retained gastric contents is concerning for patients undergoing anesthesia before endoscopy or surgery. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.
n0b134ceca0f5: The early animal communities of the Ediacaran (∼580–539 Mya) provide novel insights into how the modern biosphere operates by recording the initial ecological framework from which ecological interactions first built up. These Ediacaran communities do not have direct counterparts because they are soft-bodied, largely heterotrophic, and predator free. However, the exceptional preservation of immobile, benthic Ediacaran animals enables the resolution of their community dynamics to similar levels to those of extant benthic systems. While many of the key processes shaping the modern benthos were present in early benthic communities, the diversity of ecological interactions within communities, and the variability of these interactions through time and space, was notably simpler than that found today. In the Ediacaran, ecosystem dynamics and complexity started with reproduction and dispersal, with adaptations and responses to the environment a secondary effect, followed by direct biotic interactions. As these biotic interactions became dominant, coevolution established a tangled bank of complexity.
na60b89a039f6: Classical ecosystem theory depicts biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) as a mechanism that replenishes disturbance-driven nitrogen (N) losses, thereby alleviating N limitation and facilitating ecosystem recovery. These assumptions persist in present-day theories, models, and applications. However, disturbance regimes and environmental conditions have changed dramatically since the formation of the original BNF theories, motivating a new evaluation of the role of BNF. Focusing on forests, we find evidence that disturbance effects on BNF range from net positive to net negative and that current BNF fluxes have a limited capacity to replenish N losses if disturbances become more severe and frequent, or if they create conditions that suppress or constrain BNF. The subsequent effects of BNF on ecosystem recovery also vary. N-fixing trees and shrubs can have positive to negative effects on the recovery of carbon stocks, and under novel disturbance regimes they may alter, and even impede, forest succession. We present an updated view of BNF–recovery relationships in forest ecosystems undergoing global environmental change.
n99330c51e851: Pollen-rewarding plants face a fundamental tension: Pollen serves simultaneously as the male gametophyte and pollinator reward. Despite this apparent paradox, pollen is the second most common floral reward and the sole reward for an estimated 20,000 angiosperm species. We review the ecology and evolution of the pollen-reward strategy, synthesizing literature encompassing pollen chemistry, floral morphology, and sex allocation. We find that this reward strategy is unevenly distributed among plant families, that the resource costs of pollen rewards remain poorly characterized, and that this reward strategy may influence plant sexual-system evolution. We offer hypotheses regarding the evolution and maintenance of the pollen-reward strategy and examine the ecological and evolutionary consequences associated with its expression. We suggest that floral rewards are not isolated traits, but key elements of plant reproductive strategies, and that this perspective allows comparison among strategies and can advance our understanding of the evolutionary ecology of plant reproduction.
nbf68fb4014e5: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate. A total of 50 patients were enrolled. The primary endpoint, the premenstrual MDQ total score, was significantly ameliorated after KSS treatment. Furthermore, KSS reduced MDQ scores during the menstrual cycle. Among the MDQ subscales, KSS decreased score of pain, concentration, behavioral change, and negative feelings during the premenstrual cycle. In addition, hyperthymia reduced during the menstrual cycle. The results of the daily symptom questionnaire indicated that KSS treatment alleviated irritability, easy anger, anxiety, emotional instability, abdominal distension, coldness, and stiff shoulders.The WPAI activity impairment score was lower in the KSS group, and overall impression favoured in KSS treatment.. The only adverse event related to KSS was headache in one case. These exploratory findings suggest that KSS may improve menstrual-related symptoms in PMS.
n423eb49899e3: In Chinese higher learning institutions, students learning English as a foreign language (EFL) often demonstrate low writing self-efficacy (WSE) and poor writing competence. The present study examined the associations between the integration of peer tutoring with collaborative writing and students’ WSE and writing outcomes from a psychological perspective. A quasi-experiment was implemented for 11 weeks for 100 Chinese university students studying EFL. Changes in WSE were examined, and writing competence was assessed using tests. The results showed a notable rise in students’ WSE after the instructional intervention. The multiple linear regression analysis indicated that gains in WSE were positively associated with the writing outcome after controlling for pretest writing competence and group membership, explaining 20.2% of the total variance. These results suggest that peer-supported collaborative writing was associated with higher EFL writing competence alongside increased WSE. These findings align with theoretical justifications based on peer scaffolding and the Zone of Proximal Development, although these processes were not directly measured in the present study. These findings imply that incorporating peer tutoring into collaborative writing might be associated with the development of WSE and improved writing competence among EFL students at Chinese universities. Increased WSE appeared to be a significant, albeit partial, predictor of writing competence, highlighting the potential relevance of WSE development in peer-supported collaborative writing contexts.
n7abd8c01b967: by Abdullah M. Alharbi, Mohamed A. Awad, Mahmoud A. Attia, S.F. Mekhamer, Ahmed H. EL-Ebiary In order to address Load Frequency Control (LFC) problems in single-area and interconnected two-area power systems, this work proposes a cascaded control scheme that combines PI–PID control with the Set-Membership Affine Projection Algorithm (SMAPA). The proposed approach is evaluated under various practical operating conditions, including step load disturbances, random load variations, wind power fluctuations, and parameter uncertainty. In addition, frequency-domain stability analysis is performed to further assess the robustness of the proposed controller, while real-time validation is conducted for the two-area system to demonstrate its practical effectiveness. The proposed controller is compared with conventional PI controllers tuned using five optimization methods for the single-area system. For the two-area system, its performance is benchmarked against PID controllers designed using three optimization methods and the recently reported SPPI-based approach. The simulation results show that the proposed controller achieves lower overshoot and faster settling time in both configurations. These improvements are attributed to the integration of real-time adaptive parameter updating provided by SMAPA with the favorable dynamic characteristics of the PI–PID control structure. The results demonstrate that the proposed cascaded SMAPA-based PI–PID controller provides robust frequency regulation under different operating conditions and offers promising potential for practical interconnected power system applications.
n0e440482d05e: Entity alignment is a pivotal technology for integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs, yet most embedding-based alignment methods destroy the inherent structural embedding information of knowledge graphs when unifying cross-graph embedding spaces, resulting in limited alignment accuracy and stability. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel model for entity alignment tasks, which named as Graph Convolutional Network with Maximum Translated Similarity (GCN-MTS). GCN-MTS innovatively leverages a maximum translated similarity mechanism to optimize the adjacency matrix, degree matrix and loss function. This core design effectively maintains the original relative embedding structure of cross-graph entities during embedding space unification, which is the key improvement over existing approaches. Comprehensive experiments on 3 pairs of real-world knowledge graph dataset demonstrate the superior performance of GCN-MTS against advanced baseline methods. It achieves average performance gains of 5%–15% in Hits@1 and 4%–16% in Hits@10. Ablation results confirm that the optimized module brings a nearly 22% improvement in alignment metrics compared with the vanilla GCN. Furthermore, GCN-MTS presents excellent robustness and stability across different seed alignment quantities and seed combinations.
ndd937d2d151d: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is a major global public health threat, largely driven by the overuse and misuse of antibiotics. Tackling its animal health component is particularly difficult in low- and middle-income countries, where data and resources are limited. This qualitative study aims to explore antibiotic use (ABU) and its underlying drivers in poultry farms in Analamanga, Madagascar’s region with the highest poultry density. In April 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 79 poultry farmers (13 backyard and 66 semi-intensive), 10 animal health professionals, and 10 agrovet shop sellers. Thematic analysis was used to examine farm characteristics, poultry health management, veterinary medicine supply and use, and interactions with poultry production stakeholders, in order to identify antibiotic stewardship challenges in Madagascar's poultry sector. Backyard and semi-intensive farmers shared several features: informality (absence of farm registration, rare cooperative membership, limited training), irregular profitability, easy access to antibiotics, recurrent antibiotic misuse (for example use in poultry viral infection treatment, first-line fluoroquinolone treatments), and limited veterinary inspection by competent authorities. However, the two farmer groups differed, as semi-intensive farmers had slightly greater knowledge of ABU and ABR than backyard farmers; they primarily consulted chick and feed suppliers for health advice and medicine purchase; and they widely perceived antibiotics as essential to maintaining poultry health and productivity. Practical roadblocks to invest in preventive measures or adopt effective antibiotic stewardship (ABS) were their narrow profit margins, limited access to credit, and weak bargaining power towards poultry product buyers. Tailored approaches such as supporting professionalization of poultry sector, building capacity of chick and feed suppliers to provide training in appropriate ABU and management of flocks, flock vaccination, deworming schedules, treatment record keeping and ABS principles may enhance antibiotic usage in the Madagascar poultry sector. Future research should build on this exploratory study, which used a convenience sample of stakeholders, by examining ABU trends and drivers in Analamanga with representative sampling and rigorous quantitative validation across Madagascar’s poultry sector.
n94ba4f1b7336: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in art education raises questions about teachers’ professional security and career development. Drawing primarily on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and, in a complementary manner, on Career Construction Theory (CCT), this cross-sectional study examined associations among AI adoption, perceived job substitution risk, job insecurity, career exploration behavior, and organizational AI readiness. Survey data from 381 Chinese art teachers were analyzed using Mplus 7.4. AI adoption was positively associated with career exploration behavior. Statistically significant indirect associations were observed through job substitution risk, job insecurity, and their hypothesized sequential combination. Organizational AI readiness positively moderated the AI adoption–career exploration relationship: the association was stronger at higher readiness. COR theory offers a resource-threat interpretation of the indirect associations, while CCT highlights that career exploration may reflect threat-related coping, growth-oriented development, or both. The data did not separately measure these motivations or establish causal ordering. The findings provide context-specific insights into career exploration among art teachers during AI-related technological change.
ndec6f059c29c: Background Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease remains a significant public health threat in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Although the disease is important, its clinical characteristics are not well described in literature. This study describes the clinico-epidemiological profile of iNTS disease in Ghana aiming to bridge important knowledge gaps and inform more effective management strategies. Methods The study spanned 8 years and utilized selected fever surveillance sites in Ghana. Patients with fever and/or history of fever for ≥ 3 consecutive days within the week prior to visit were approached and blood sample taken after consenting for investigations including blood culture. iNTS isolates were recovered using BACTEC blood culture, identified by Analytical Profile Index (API), sero-grouped using the Kauffmann–White scheme and confirmed by Illumina whole genome sequencing. Conditional logistic regression was used to assess associations between clinical and laboratory features and iNTS blood culture positivity in a 1:3 age-, sex-, and residence-matched case–control analysis. Results Of 271 blood-culture-derived bacterial pathogens, 15.5% (42/271) were identified as iNTS making it the second most common cause of bacteremia. iNTS disease exhibited seasonality with peak detections coinciding with the rainy seasons in Ghana. 23.7% (9/38) of iNTS isolates were multidrug-resistant (MDR), of which 5.3% (2/38) were extensively drug-resistant including resistance to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Several factors showed crude associations with iNTS disease; however, only anaemia retained its association after adjustment of other factors (aOR=2.41 p = 0.030). Conclusion iNTS is a major cause of bloodstream infections with the highest burden in children under 5 years of age with susceptibility to the infection amplified by anaemia. The Salmonella serovars involved are increasingly becoming multidrug-resistant, including resistance to critical antibiotics.
n7e9afde600c3: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide. Sudden cardiac death (SCD) accounts for roughly 50% of all cardiac deaths. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is widely used for diagnosing cardiac disease. However, the complexity of interpretation limits the ECG’s efficacy. Modern deep learning methods can assist clinicians in diagnosis. We applied Neural Architecture Search (NAS) to identify optimal deep learning architectures for classifying cardiac arrhythmias with ECGs. We applied the Differentiable Architecture Search strategy to an AutoFormer search and trained, validated, and tested the resulting model on the PhysioNet Challenge 2021 (PC21) dataset (n = 88,253 from three continents). We optimised hyperparameters on the NAS output, exploring input patch size, class weighting, and loss function. The PC21 metric and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) are the performance metrics. The NAS converged towards minimal architectural configurations (embedding dimension: 384, depth: 4, self-attention heads: 4, MLP ratio: 1) with a validation and test PC21 metric of 0.66 (PC21 winner: 0.63). The NAS-created network achieved an AUROC of 0.97 and a PC21 metric of 0.72 during testing (PC21 winner: 0.69). We tested the PC21 winner architecture (1D-convolutional neural network with attention mechanism) without the attention mechanism and with the NAS-suggested architecture of 4 self-attention heads (instead of 8). The architecture without the attention mechanism performed similarly to the one with 8 self-attention heads (AUROC: 0.90, PC21 metric: 0.69). The architecture with 4 self-attention heads scored an AUROC of 0.91 and improved the PC21 metric to 0.71. The attention mechanism visualisation for two SCD-related arrhythmias (premature ventricular contractions and prolonged QT-interval) showed more clinically relevant attention for the 4-self-attention-head architectures. We interpret architectural simplicity as driving performance in arrhythmia classification. The self-attention mechanism can autonomously abstract clinical representations, simplifying clinical deployment by eliminating the need for an explicit feature-extraction pipeline.
n1958ae4776a4: by Mohammed AL Awadh The rapid growth of e-commerce has intensified competition among online retailers, making e-service quality increasingly important for building customer trust, satisfaction, and sustainable customer–platform relationships. This study examines the relationships among e-service quality, customer trust, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty using a second-order Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) framework. The five SERVQUAL dimensions such as empathy, responsiveness, reliability, assurance, and tangibles were modeled as first-order constructs reflecting the higher-order construct of service quality. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 402 respondents with prior online-shopping experience. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and SEM were employed to assess the measurement and structural models. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and overall model fit. The structural results showed that service quality significantly and positively influenced customer trust and customer satisfaction, while customer trust significantly enhanced satisfaction. Trust also partially mediated the relationship between service quality and satisfaction, indicating that e-service quality improves satisfaction both directly and through increased customer confidence. The SERVQUAL dimensions contributed positively to overall service quality, with responsiveness and assurance showing particularly strong contributions, while empathy exhibited a comparatively moderate contribution. In contrast, customer loyalty had no significant direct effect on trust or satisfaction, and its indirect effect on satisfaction through trust was also nonsignificant. These findings demonstrate that reliable, responsive, secure, and well-designed digital services are important for strengthening trust and satisfaction in competitive e-commerce environments. By identifying trust as a key mechanism linking multidimensional e-service quality with customer satisfaction, the study contributes to SERVQUAL and digital-commerce literature and provides implications for the economic and relational sustainability of e-commerce platforms through more resilient and durable customer relationships.
n12493723efb4: Background Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke. Aim To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke. Methods A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS. Discussion This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.
ndf5e02df0f8d: Background/Objectives Low vitamin D status is frequently reported among athletes, but whether vitamin D supplementation improves physical performance in football players remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vitamin D supplementation on serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentration, jump performance, sprint performance, aerobic capacity, and muscular performance in association football and futsal players. Methods PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 31 May 2026. Controlled intervention studies comparing vitamin D supplementation with control conditions were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges’ g and pooled using random-effects meta-analyses. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261430873). Results Eleven reports representing nine independent studies and 312 players were included. In RCT-only primary analyses, vitamin D supplementation was associated with higher circulating 25(OH)D concentrations (g = 1.41, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.92; I² = 58.0%). Pooled effects were not statistically significant for jump performance (g = 0.21, 95% CI −0.10 to 0.53), sprint performance (g = −0.03, 95% CI −0.40 to 0.34), aerobic capacity (g = 0.00, 95% CI −0.45 to 0.45), or muscular performance (g = 0.19, 95% CI −0.14 to 0.51). The certainty of evidence was low for circulating 25(OH)D, jump performance, and muscular performance, and very low for sprint performance and aerobic capacity. Conclusions Vitamin D supplementation was associated with increased circulating 25(OH)D concentrations, whereas current evidence is insufficient to support a consistent improvement in physical performance. Given the low to very low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials using standardized, football-relevant performance tests are warranted.
nb4feef1b8622: Background In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment. Methodology A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18–80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269. Results The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant. Conclusion Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.
n3f570a0d54c3: Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020–2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. To maintain industry confidentiality, diagnostic data from these separate facilities were fully aggregated and evaluated across three broad macro-regional surveillance zones. A total of 5,235 fish displaying clinical signs underwent diagnostic necropsy. Presumptive bacterial identification was conducted using phenotypic profiling through the API 20E system, and organ touch-imprint cytology. Six distinct bacterial species were isolated from positive clinical individuals, recovering a total of 2,490 isolates. Across the recorded outbreak events, etiological agents were ranked as primary drivers as follows: Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida (48.80%; N = 365), Tenacibaculum maritimum (35.83%; N = 268), Vibrio (Listonella) anguillarum (9.49%; N = 71), V. harveyi (3.74%; N = 28), V. ordalii (1.20%; N = 9), and V. alginolyticus (0.94%; N = 7). This hierarchy directly mirrored the overall bacterial isolation frequency, where P. damselae subsp. piscicida showed the highest relative distribution rate (46.18%; n = 1,150), followed by T. maritimum (34.10%; n = 849). Significantly lower isolation rates were recorded for V. (Listonella) anguillarum (11.41%; n = 284), V. harveyi (5.26%; n = 131), V. ordalii (1.77%; n = 44), and V. alginolyticus (1.29%; n = 32). n25e5fcaec05b: Separate tests are usually used to assess an athlete's ability to meet the aerobic and anaerobic demands of ball sports. These tests often compromise ecological validity by relying on linear runs and sprints rather than multidirectional reactive agility. This study investigated the correlations between a novel motor-cognitive reactive agility (RA) test and aerobic and anaerobic performance indices. Twenty-two trained participants (V˙O2max: 56 ± 6.4 ml ∙ kg-1 ∙ min-1) performed a treadmill ramp test to determine maximum oxygen uptake (V˙O2max), a running-based anaerobic sprint test (RAST) to determine peak power output (PPO), average power putput (POAV), fatigue index (FI) and anaerobic capacity (AC) and a motor-cognitive RA test on the SKILLCOURT. The RA test required participants to perform four 150 m maximal multidirectional change of directions runs with a break of 30 s. Running time, heart rate and power output were determined for all runs and correlated to V˙O2max and anaerobic performance indicators. Running time of the 4th SKILLCOURT run was correlated to V˙O2max (r20 = −0.80, p 20 = 0.72, p < 0.001). n251890f0042e: by Bria L. Bartsch, Amanda N. Engler, Sandra A. n48d47bb3ddd2: by Lijuan Zhang This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). The NFTSM guarantees singularity free finite time convergence of the tracking errors. The RBFNN approximates the slowly varying unknown dynamics, while the FTDO compensates online for the neural approximation residual and fast varying disturbances in a cascaded “coarse to fine” manner. Lyapunov-based Extensive co‑simulations with MATLAB/Simulink, conducted under double lane change and sinusoidal path scenarios with simultaneous road friction drops and stochastic lateral wind gusts, demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional nonsingular terminal sliding mode control and disturbance observer based sliding mode control in terms of tracking accuracy, convergence speed, and chattering suppression.
nb01ed978fd30: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in working-age populations. Astrocyte senescence is highly prevalent in DR, but the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR. Methods Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA). Protein and mRNA levels of key factors were detected by Western blot and RT-qPCR. Astrocytes and retinal microvascular endothelial cells were co-cultured in Transwell systems to assess paracrine regulation on endothelial migration, proliferation, and apoptosis. Results High glucose induced astrocyte senescence, inflammatory activation, and downregulation of GDNF and NRTN, accompanied by elevated HIF-1α and PPAR-γ, and reduced SIRT1 expression and autophagy activity. Inhibiting HIF-1α or activating SIRT1 attenuated senescence, apoptosis, and inflammation, restored autophagy, and upregulated GDNF/NRTN secretion. HIF-1α negatively regulated SIRT1 expression via PPAR-γ. Senescent astrocytes impaired endothelial function through reduced GDNF/NRTN; overexpression of GDNF or NRTN in astrocytes preserved endothelial migration and proliferation, and inhibited apoptosis. Conclusion HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis mediates high glucose-induced astrocyte senescence via autophagy dysfunction. Senescent astrocytes disrupt retinal endothelial homeostasis by reducing GDNF/NRTN secretion. Targeting this axis may represent a novel neurovascular protective therapeutic strategy for DR.
n351a601e0d7e: Background HIV-related stigma remains a significant barrier to prevention and treatment efforts in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. This study assessed HIV knowledge and stigmatizing attitudes among United Arab Emirates (UAE) residents. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted across the UAE between January and March 2025. A total of 1,211 eligible adult residents were recruited through convenience sampling. Demographic analyses included all 1,211 participants, while HIV knowledge and stigma analyses included 1,171 participants with analyzable outcome data. The questionnaire assessed demographics, HIV transmission knowledge, and stigmatizing attitudes using the Stigmatizing Attitudes Towards People Living with HIV/AIDS Scale (SAT-PLWHA-S). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate analyses, and multiple linear regression. Results Among the 1,211 participants included in the study, 1,171 contributed analyzable data to the HIV knowledge and stigma analyses. While 96.4% had heard of HIV/AIDS and demonstrated moderately high transmission knowledge (mean score: 75.5%), significant misconceptions persisted, particularly regarding condom effectiveness (60.5% overestimated risk). Strong stigmatizing attitudes emerged, especially regarding criminalization of transmission (79.6% support) and moralistic views. Higher knowledge correlated with less stigma (r = 0.347, p < 0.001), though nationality, language preference, and knowing someone with HIV were stronger predictors. Only 6.2% knew someone with HIV. Conclusions Despite adequate basic knowledge, significant HIV-related stigma persists in the UAE, driven by cultural and moral perspectives. Comprehensive interventions combining education, contact-based strategies, and policy reform are needed to reduce stigma and improve HIV prevention outcomes.
n837c38b621f3: Background Vaginal fistula (VF), particularly vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), remains a significant reproductive health challenge in many low-resource settings, including the Kpandai District of Ghana. Aim This study explored the lived experiences of women diagnosed with vesicovaginal fistula in the Kpandai District of Ghana, focusing on their physical, emotional, and social challenges, as well as coping strategies. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using in-depth interviews with ten women with clinically confirmed VVF. Participants were initially identified through a district health facility and subsequently recruited using a combination of purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically. Results Prolonged and obstructed labour—often occurring at home—emerged as the primary reported cause of VVF. Cultural beliefs, gender-based decision-making dynamics, limited access to healthcare, and financial constraints were key barriers to timely medical intervention. Consequences included persistent urinary incontinence, social stigma, emotional trauma, marital dissolution (reported by eight participants), loss of livelihood, and social isolation. Coping strategies included frequent washing, use of absorbent materials, and reliance on perfumes or herbal remedies. Conclusions Vesicovaginal fistula remains a devastating yet largely preventable condition in rural Ghana. The findings highlight the need to strengthen maternal health services, improve timely referral systems, and integrate psychosocial support within community-based care frameworks.

n3db3869c5a76: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.
nd702f2f76044: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.
nb81a75e81f0b: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.
n7c62b94c98b9: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). The 3.0-µm-pored membrane induced an epithelial structure with three distinct states: stratified KCs above the membrane, KCs showing EMT within the micropores, and a new stratified epithelium under the membrane. The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.
n2217a2c6fa0a: A coordinated response to stress is crucial for promoting the short- and long-term health of an organism. The perception of stress, frequently through the nervous system, can lead to physiological changes that are fundamental to maintaining homeostasis. Thus, it is imperative to identify which components of this response promote longevity. Here, we interrogate the cell-nonautonomous signaling pathway downstream of genetic activation of the hypoxic response. We find that HIF-1-mediated signaling in ADF serotonergic neurons is both necessary and sufficient for lifespan extension. Signaling through the serotonin receptor SER-7 in the GABAergic RIS interneurons is necessary in this process. Our findings also highlight the involvement of additional neural signaling molecules, including the neurotransmitters tyramine and GABA, and the neuropeptide NLP-17, in mediating longevity effects. Finally, we demonstrate that oxygen- and carbon-dioxide-sensing neurons act downstream of HIF-1 in this circuit. Together, these insights demonstrate a circuit for how genetic induction of the hypoxic response cell-nonautonomously modifies aging and suggests valuable targets for modulating aging in mammals.
n1f5bab73c569: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior. While traditional accounts treat controllability as a fixed property of the environment, we argue that real-world controllability often depends on the effort, time, and money we are able and willing to invest. In such cases, controllability can be said to be elastic to invested resources. Here, we propose that inferring this elasticity is essential for efficient resource allocation, and thus, elasticity misestimations result in maladaptive behavior. To test this hypothesis, we developed a novel treasure hunt game where participants encountered environments with varying degrees of controllability and elasticity. Across two pre-registered studies (N=514), we first demonstrate that people infer elasticity and adapt their resource allocation accordingly. We then present a computational model that explains how people make this inference and identify individual elasticity biases that lead to suboptimal resource allocation. Finally, we show that overestimation of elasticity is associated with elevated psychopathology involving an impaired sense of control. These findings establish the elasticity of control as a distinct cognitive construct guiding adaptive behavior and a computational marker for control-related maladaptive behavior.
n1086c8226d15: Scope taking is one of the most characteristic, distinctive, and ubiquitous phenomena in natural language. When an expression takes scope, it combines with surrounding material as its semantic argument. For instance, in Amy gave everyone a book , the semantic argument of everyone is an abstraction over the entire rest of the sentence, namely, λ x . Amy gave x a book , the property an individual has if Amy gave that individual a book. This ability to operate on surrounding context dramatically enriches (and complicates) the ways that meanings can be expressed. Although there are many formal theories of scope taking, Quantifier Raising—often thought of as a covert (silent) version of overt syntactic movement—is by far the dominant approach. There are many constraints on the availability of scope taking that depend on the identity of the scope taker as well as on its surrounding context.
nd217c2aa324d: A speech sample can be morphed from one voice to another by computing a sufficiently detailed time-frequency parameterization of the signal, optionally decomposing it into speaker-dependent and speaker-independent signal components, editing the parameterization or signal components, and then generating a speech signal based on the edited parameterization. Fine-grained control of time-frequency parameters has found applications in the scientific study of speech perception and in artistic applications such as voiceover and music. Coarse-grained control of speaker identity, emotion, and second-language accent have been applied to various tasks, including the training of speech recognizers and speaker anonymization.
n4dbe9ebfb917: Singular they is valuable to psycholinguistic research because it has a long-standing usage in English that is currently undergoing changes, both in how often it is used and in what conditions. We suggest that there are two main varieties of singular they that currently differ in acceptability and processing characteristics. Psycholinguistic research shows that singular they is viewed as more acceptable and used more easily within a supportive context that helps to make the pronoun pragmatically appropriate.
n94a2ed0497d5: Biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA) is a major component of atmospheric particulate matter and is expected to become increasingly important as wildfire activity increases. Field measurements indicate that atmospheric BBOA is often more viscous than unaged laboratory BBOA. Laboratory measurements further suggest that aged BBOA commonly exists in highly viscous or glassy states in the free troposphere and may exhibit mixing times exceeding one hour. We also highlight future research directions.

n469f4b242f9c: Many bacteria form spores to endure unfavorable conditions. While Firmicutes generate endospores through cell division, sporulation in non-Firmicutes remains less understood. The Gram-negative bacterium Myxococcus xanthus undergoes sporulation through two distinct mechanisms: rapid sporulation triggered by chemical induction and slow sporulation driven by starvation, both occurring independently of cell division. Instead, these processes depend on the complete degradation of the peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall by two lytic transglycosylases (LTGs), LtgA and LtgB. Remarkably, LtgB programs the pace of PG degradation by LtgA during rapid sporulation, ensuring a controlled process that prevents abrupt PG breakdown and the formation of non-resistant pseudospores. In addition to regulation between LTGs, PG degradation is also influenced by its synthesis; cells exhibiting increased muropeptide production often circumvent sporulation. These findings not only reveal novel mechanisms of bacterial sporulation but also shed light on the regulatory network governing PG dynamics.
na969e165a2fb: The ability to represent absences is fundamental to human perception and cognition. Sensitivity to non-numerical absences depends on inferring a lack of sensory evidence, enabling the recognition of a lack of environmental resources or other objects. In turn, encoding numerical absence as a concept – in the form of the number zero – has enabled a multitude of technological and mathematical advances. Whether perceptual and conceptual absences rely on overlapping or distinct neural representations in the human brain, however, remains unknown. We employed three different tasks together with magnetoencephalography to characterise neural representations of absence evoked within perceptual and numerical domains. Using multivariate decoding and Bayes factor analyses, we replicate previous findings of shared representations of numerical absence across symbolic and non-symbolic formats. In contrast, we show that these representations of numerical absence are distinct from those evoked by non-numerical absences. This result held even after controlling for stimulus-level confounds which generate surface-level similarities between perceptual absences and non-symbolic empty sets. Our results extend a boundary between perception and cognition to the domain of absence and provide insight into the different mechanisms employed by the human brain to both perceive and conceive of absences.
nf6c003701d7c: Heartbeat and behavior are tightly coordinated during defensive states, yet the neuronal mechanisms linking threat processing to cardiac modulation—and the potential contribution of cardiac dynamics to behavioral output—remain poorly understood. Here, using simultaneous recordings of heartbeat and behavior in tethered Drosophila, we show that mechanical threat triggers locomotion together with rapid cardiac deceleration. We identify two pairs of dopaminergic neurons, termed DA-WED neurons, that mediate this cardiac response. Silencing these neurons markedly attenuates threat-induced cardiac deceleration, whereas optogenetic activation induces cardiac deceleration in the absence of threat. Two-photon calcium imaging further shows that DA-WED neurons are activated by mechanical threat, and manipulating their activity bidirectionally modulates threat-induced locomotion. Linking cardiac dynamics to behavior, direct optogenetic manipulation of cardiomyocytes that quantitatively reproduces threat-evoked cardiac deceleration is accompanied by increased locomotion. Together, these results identify a dopaminergic descending pathway that links threat processing to cardiac modulation and suggest that cardiac dynamics may contribute to shaping defensive behavior.
na0ecbf1cd45a: Blood progenitors are regulated by a variety of systemic and nutritional cues from their environment. In the Drosophila lymph gland (LG), the Posterior Signaling Center acts as a stem cell niche striking a balance between progenitors and differentiated blood cells. Autophagy is a vital cellular process that maintains homeostasis by removing unnecessary or dysfunctional cell components through autophagic degradation and recycling. Here, using genetic perturbation analysis, we show that autophagy plays a critical role in regulating LG blood cell homeostasis. General control non-derepressible 5 (Gcn5), a histone acetyltransferase, is expressed in the primary LG lobe, and modulation of Gcn5 levels perturbs LG homeostasis. Our results show that hemocyte-specific Gcn5 modulation controls autophagic flux in the hemocytes. Furthermore, we show that modulation of mTORC1 activity can perturb hematopoiesis. Our results indicate that organismal Gcn5 levels respond to dietary shifts and are modulated by mTORC1 signaling. Chemical intervention shows that mTORC1 overrides the effect exerted by Gcn5 in regulating LG hematopoiesis. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that Gcn5 and mTORC1 regulate autophagy to maintain blood cell homeostasis in Drosophila.
ne93437c9d17a: The differential microtubule organization in axons and dendrites underlies neuronal polarity and developmental processes, like neurite pruning. How neurons achieve their specific microtubule organization during development is an area of active research, and it has been especially hard to explain how dendritic microtubules are oriented with their plus ends toward the soma. Transient microtubule nucleation from tips of early growing dendrites has been proposed as a mechanism that would explain how this orientation is set up. In a survey for cytoskeletal regulators involved in dendrite pruning and microtubule organization in Drosophila, we found the spectraplakin Short stop (Shot), an actin/microtubule crosslinker. Loss of Shot causes microtubule orientation defects already during early dendrite development, when Shot is transiently recruited to tips of growing dendrites via its actin-binding domain. Genetic and functional evidence suggests that Shot’s primary function in this process is to locally stabilize microtubules. We also provide evidence for an independent, developmentally transient microtubule nucleation mechanism. Our data highlight the importance of transient and localized microtubule regulation for dendritic microtubule organization.
n01709f8f6122: Food formulation requires balancing taste, nutrition, sustainability, and cost. Traditionally, new foods have emerged through empirical experimentation, expert intuition, and iterative refinement. Now, artificial intelligence (AI) offers the opportunity to accelerate this process. Yet despite rapid advances across food science, most AI applications remain isolated prediction and optimization tasks rather than parts of a broader scientific approach. Here we integrate these emerging technologies into a unified framework—the generative science of food formulation—in which digital food representations enable AI to predict, discover, generate, organize, simulate, and optimize. We illustrate this approach through sustainability and nutrition, where generative AI transforms environmental and nutritional metrics from post hoc evaluation criteria into explicit design objectives. Finally, we identify the data, models, benchmarks, and automation that will establish computational food design as a rigorous scientific discipline. Together, these advances have the potential to transform food formulation from an empirical discipline into a generative science.
n02e420da49e1: Circadian rhythms regulate the time of day at which various physiological processes take place, including the functions of the kidney. This regulation is made possible by key transcriptional regulators: the core molecular circadian clock, which mediates expression of clock-controlled genes on a 24-h cycle. The present landscape of circadian rhythm research in the kidney spans impacts on the clinical level as well as in basic research, where its role in individual kidney cell types, disease states, and the impacts of environmental stressors is being studied. Recent research has also identified sex differences, cross talk between various tissues, and immune signaling as important considerations for understanding the circadian clocks within the kidney. This review synthesizes the current knowledge of circadian rhythms of the kidney in regard to these issues and stresses the importance of time of day in research as well as in patient health.
nd4adcccfda3e: Probiotics are widely used live microbial supplements intended to promote human health, yet their clinical benefits remain inconsistent and often strain-specific. Most currently available probiotics are derived from Lactobacillus , Bifidobacterium , and Saccharomyces species originally isolated from fermented foods or human microbiota. Preclinical studies suggest that these organisms may influence host physiology through several mechanisms, including antimicrobial activity, toxin inhibition, strengthening of intestinal barrier function, modulation of immune responses, and signaling along the gut–brain axis. However, translation of these mechanisms into consistent clinical benefit has been limited by heterogeneity in probiotic strains, dosing, and study design. Emerging evidence also highlights potential unintended consequences of probiotic use, including rare infections in vulnerable patients, alterations of microbiome recovery after antibiotics, and possible interactions with host metabolism or medications. Recent advances in microbiome research have supported the development of next-generation probiotics and engineered microbial therapeutics, representing a shift toward more targeted and mechanistically informed live microbial therapies.
nbd4a9cbb9721: Flow disturbances in the smallest blood vessels of the brain, the capillaries, have long been considered a potential cause of brain dysfunction. Advances in optical microscopes for in vivo imaging, primarily high-spatiotemporal-resolution optical coherence tomography and two-photon microscopy, have recently enabled detailed studies of these capillary stalling events in both healthy and diseased mice. In this review, we describe these imaging approaches to quantify capillary stalling, identifying strengths and weaknesses of different methods. We then review recent findings on the incidence, molecular and cellular causes, and physiological and neurological consequences of capillary stalling across multiple mouse models of brain disease, including Alzheimer's disease, stroke, and traumatic brain injury. We conclude by suggesting necessary next steps in instrumentation and analysis for studying capillary stalling, as well as how to address key unanswered questions about underlying mechanisms for capillary stalling in the brain and how this phenomenon may impact disease progression and cognitive function.
